name: Shâhî (Prince Bayezid)
bio: Prince Bayezid, a son of Sultan Suleyman I, led an unsuccessful revolt against his brother Selim, was defeated on the plain of Qonya and fled to Persia.
The poems here are taken from E. J. W. Gibb's Ottoman Poems (1882), the first English verse translations of Ottoman poetry; dates and biographical details follow Gibb's Biographical Notices.

poems.title: With Longing Fond and Vain
poems.author: Shâhî (Prince Bayezid)
poems.text:
With longing fond and vain, why should I make my soul to mourn?
One trace of love of earth holds not my heart — all is forsworn.

There ready stands the caravan, to Death's dim realms addrest,
E'en now the tinkling of its bells down on my ears is borne.

Come then, O bird, my soul, be still, disquiet leave far off;
See, how this cage, the body, is with years and suffering worn.

But yet, to weary, wasted, sin-stained Shâhî, what of fear?
Since Thou'rt the God of Love, the helping Friend of those forlorn!
